title: A delivery spends fewer turns, and the gates get the evidence handed to them
summary: The 2.32.0 run on the fixed fixture priced a delivery for the first time: $4.82 for two work items, $2.41 an item, and the money is not where the attention has been. The orchestrator spent 57% of it and the two builders 36%, while both gate reviewers together came to 6.5%. Cost here is context multiplied by turns — cache reads of the conversation so far are about 90% of every billed token, and cache traffic (reads plus creation) nearly all of every dollar, so spending less means taking fewer turns at a smaller context, not writing shorter answers. This binder does both halves. The gates get the evidence handed to them, which is the change that was asked for: every dispatch brief now carries the oracle's evidence record, the work item's own JSON, and the list of changed files, so a reviewer stops re-deriving what the oracle already established. The larger savings come from the measurement-directed items — an orientation packet the orchestrator and each builder read once instead of discovering by hand, a merge-queue command that turns five orchestrator turns per item into one, and a miner that can finally report context and cost per role. The target is written down and is not an oracle: at least 40% lower cost per item against the 2.32.0 baseline of $2.41 on fixture-v1 (the comparison is on the unrounded cost_usd_per_item against 0.60 × $2.41 = $1.446 — $1.44 is the largest displayed-to-cents value guaranteed under the line, since a displayed $1.45 may sit either side of the unrounded $1.446), judged by the perf-fixture-cost-baseline card run after the next release under the card's own comparison precondition — the same resolved model-ID set as the 2.32.0 baseline; a run on a different model set is inconclusive for the target, not a pass or a fail.
motivation: The measured 2.32.0 fixture run (run root /tmp/karta-bench.OJckW8, session f6f1b20b, 2 items, $4.8163, 7.0 wall minutes) shows spend concentrated in the orchestrator (57%) and the builders (36%) with the two gates at 6.5%, and cache-read input tokens at ~90% of the billed tokens (cache traffic — reads plus creation — is nearly all of the dollar cost) — so the cheapest change is fewer turns at a smaller context, and the gate-brief change is one item of five rather than the whole answer.

included: benchmarks/perf/mine_fixture.py — per-role context and cost accounting: assistant messages deduplicated by message id, cache-read and cache-creation tokens per role, context tokens per item, and — given the run's headless result line — dollars per role and per item; plus recognition of the new merge-queue invocation so the card's PRIMARY structural counts stay comparable across the release that introduces it

work_items.title: The cost miner learns to price a run per role
work_items.summary: The fixed-fixture miner starts reporting how much context each role reads and what each role costs, so a release is compared on the number that actually drives spend.
work_items.contract: Extend benchmarks/perf/mine_fixture.py, its card, and its bench-spec entry so the vector reports the cost driver rather than a proxy for it. Nothing here changes what the miner already emits; every existing key keeps its meaning and its value. (1) PER-ROLE CONTEXT ACCOUNTING. For every context in a run — the main session transcript plus each `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` — walk the assistant messages and DEDUPLICATE THEM BY MESSAGE ID before summing usage: the transcript writes one line per content block, so the same message's `usage` block repeats and a naive sum double-counts. Emit, keyed by the same role names the file already uses (`orchestrator`, `builder`, `acceptance-reviewer`, `safety-auditor`, `other`), a `per_role_usage` map of {messages, input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, output_tokens, avg_context_tokens}, where avg_context_tokens is that role's mean per-message context size (read + creation + input). (2) `context_tokens_per_item` = the sum of cache_read_input_tokens plus cache_creation_input_tokens plus input_tokens (the uncached remainder — `per_role_usage` carries it as `input_tokens` too) across all roles, divided by the number of work items in the run's binder(s) — the same denominator the existing per-item metrics use. (3) COST, WHEN THE RUN SAYS SO. Add a `--result FILE` argument naming the run's headless stream file (`run<i>.jsonl` at the run root). When its final result line carries `modelUsage`, emit `cost_usd_per_role` and `cost_usd_per_item` by this exact formula, per model m with recorded cost C_m: a role's weight W_role,m = cache_read_input_tokens×1 + input_tokens×10 + cache_creation_input_tokens×12.5 + output_tokens×50 (the list-price ratios Anthropic publishes for every current model: cache read = 10% of input, cache creation = 125% of input, output = 5× input; the weights are constants in the miner with this comment, never a rate table, and the absolute price always comes from modelUsage); cost_role = Σ_m [ C_m × W_role,m / (Σ_roles W_role,m) ] — the denominator is PER MODEL: each model's recorded cost is shared out by that model's own role weights, never a global weight pool; cost_usd_per_item = Σ_roles cost_role ÷ items. MODEL IDENTITY IS NORMALIZED: the transcripts report `claude-opus-5` while the headless result keys modelUsage as `claude-opus-5[1m]` with `canonicalModel: claude-opus-5` (measured on the 2.32.0 run) — match a transcript model to a modelUsage entry by the entry's `canonicalModel` when present, else by the key with any `[...]` suffix stripped; a transcript model with no matching entry, an entry no role used (Σ_roles W = 0), or two modelUsage entries normalizing to the SAME canonical model, is a LOUD failure (nonzero exit naming the model), never a silent zero or a silent merge. The self-test covers the `[1m]`-suffixed alias shape. By construction the role costs sum to the run's total_cost_usd (assert it within $0.01). When `--result` is absent or the line carries no `modelUsage`, both keys are `null` and the miner says so in a `cost_note`; it never estimates a price from a rate table. (4) THE NEW MERGE-QUEUE INVOCATION. `_revalidation_before_merge` today credits an evidenced re-validation only when a `run_oracle.py` Bash call precedes a `git merge` of an item branch. Once the merge-queue item lands, the orchestrator runs neither — both happen inside the script — so a main-session Bash command containing `merge_item.py` counts as ONE item merge AND ONE evidenced re-validation. Match that form FIRST and let it consume the line — the real orchestrator line is `python3 …/merge_item.py merge …` and contains no literal `git merge`; a line that invokes `merge_item.py` with the `merge` subcommand token is counted from its RESULT, not its text: merge_item.py always prints one fixed-shape JSON object per invocation, so the miner counts one merge with one evidenced re-validation for each result JSON in the line's paired tool result whose `halted_at` is null AND whose `skipped_done` is false — a skip landed nothing, exactly like a halt — a loop line with three successful invocations carries three result objects and counts three, a halted invocation counts nothing because it landed nothing, and when no paired tool result can be located the fallback is one per `merge`-subcommand invocation token — never two per result, and never also arms a stale `run_oracle.py` credit; `close-wave` and `tag-wave` lines also mention the script and count as NOTHING (self-tested as a negative control); a legacy `git merge` line without `merge_item.py` keeps today's counting. Without this the card's PRIMARY structural counts would read as a regression to zero the quarter the script ships, which is the one failure mode this rule exists to prevent. (5) BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY IS PART OF THE CONTRACT. `EXPECTED_FIXTURE` and `check_fixture()` are imported by benchmarks/probes/perf-fixture-cost-baseline.py, which compares only the keys the expectation names; adding keys must not change any pinned value, and the probe's own `--self-test` must still pass. (6) THE CARD AND THE SPEC. In benchmarks/perf/perf-fixture-cost-baseline.md steps 6 and 7, and in the mirrored `procedure` and `metric` text of the `perf-fixture-cost-baseline` entry in benchmarks/bench-spec.json, add median `context-tokens/item` and `cost-USD/item` to SECONDARY under the SAME rule the existing SECONDARY metrics carry — flag only when the median shifts more than 25% AND the resolved model-ID set is unchanged. Say plainly why they are there: cache reads are about 90% of the billed tokens and cache traffic nearly all of the spend, so output tokens per item do not measure what costs money. The literal `cache read` must appear in both files. Keep the two texts saying the same thing — the card is the readable copy, the spec entry is the machine-readable one. (7) RE-MINE OR SAY WHY NOT. Both committed result files record a `run_root`, and both COMPLETE runs' isolated transcripts existed when this binder was planned (/tmp/karta-bench.ZbSxz3 and /tmp/karta-bench.OJckW8, each holding `claude-config/projects/<mangled>/<session>.jsonl` plus its `subagents/` directory, with `run1.jsonl` at the run root for `--result`). If they still exist at build time (the run's `run_root/run1.jsonl`), re-mining is MANDATORY and the oracle enforces it — a deferral note is accepted only for a run whose transcripts are gone; and re-mining is PROVEN, not asserted — the oracle re-runs the miner on each surviving run's own transcript (`metrics.session`) with `--result <run_root>/run1.jsonl` and `--binders <every *.json under the run root's repo/.karta/binders/ and its archive/>` — the existing repeatable `--binders` argument, pinned here so an implementer never has to re-derive it from the oracle shell and requires the four new fields it emits to equal the committed ones, so placeholder numbers cannot pass; re-mine the COMPLETE run of each file and add the new fields to its `metrics`, changing no existing value. If they are gone, the four new fields must be ABSENT from that file's metrics (an unverifiable number is worse than none) and add one `harness_notes` entry to each file that names `context_tokens_per_item` and states that the new fields start at the next release — the oracle accepts either, and accepts nothing else. (8) SELF-TEST ADDITIONS, both with a negative control, in the house pattern ([PASS]/[FAIL] lines and an N/N summary): the embedded headless synthetic gains usage blocks written as DUPLICATED content-block lines for one message id, and the test asserts that the naive sum does NOT equal the deduplicated value and that the deduplicated value is the right one; a synthetic two-role, two-model result (one modelUsage entry per model, two roles with different token mixes) whose per-role allocations are asserted to exact expected values and whose role costs sum to the recorded costUSD, with the no-`--result` path asserted to yield null costs and a `cost_note`; and a synthetic main-session Bash line invoking `merge_item.py merge` is asserted to yield `merge_revalidations` of one evidenced re-validation and one item merge, while the same run with the call removed — or with only `merge_item.py close-wave` and `merge_item.py tag-wave` lines — yields zero of each, a single line whose paired tool result carries two success result JSONs yields two, and one whose result JSON carries a non-null `halted_at` — or `skipped_done: true` with `halted_at` null — yields zero; and a synthetic context with nonzero read, creation AND plain input tokens is asserted to yield an independently computed exact `context_tokens_per_item` and `per_role_usage.input_tokens`, with a negative control that drops the input term and must not match. (9) NOT IN SCOPE HERE: benchmarks/flow/check_contradictions.py is a doctrine-contradiction ledger that requires `--repo` and `--out` and reads no benchmark metric — this item changes no doctrine file, so it is not part of this oracle. (10) ADDITIVE ONLY, CHECKED RECURSIVELY: the oracle walks each committed result file against its `main` version — the pre-delivery baseline; HEAD would be the merge commit itself at merge-time re-validation, making the check vacuous — and fails if any pre-existing key was removed or any pre-existing value changed at ANY depth — top-level fields (plugin_sha, fixture_sha256, aggregate) included; a re-mine may only add dictionary keys, and `harness_notes` may only grow by appending. A re-mine counts only when all four new metrics (per_role_usage, context_tokens_per_item, cost_usd_per_role, cost_usd_per_item) are present on every COMPLETE run; the fallback note must name context_tokens_per_item and say the fields start at the next release.

work_items.title: One command tells the orchestrator where the delivery stands, and one tells a builder what its item is
work_items.summary: Two new scripts answer in a single JSON packet everything the delivery orchestrator and each build worker currently discover by hand, and the two skills are told to read the packet instead of searching.
work_items.contract: Two NEW pure-stdlib scripts on the house pattern (argparse, `--self-test` printing [PASS]/[FAIL] lines and an N/N summary, exit 0/1, invoked as `python3 <path>`, non-executable mode like their siblings), plus the doctrine that makes the orchestrator and the builder read them. (1) skills/karta-deliver/scripts/deliver_preflight.py — `--binder PATH [--repo DIR]` prints ONE JSON object on stdout with at least these top-level keys: `validator` (the result of running skills/karta-plan/scripts/validate_binder.py, resolved as ../../karta-plan/scripts/validate_binder.py relative to THIS script's own location and executed with the current interpreter — the validator is zero-dependency stdlib, so `python3` and `uv run --script` behave identically; carry its exit status and its output; a validator that exits nonzero ALSO sets the packet's `halt` field — an invalid binder is a stop, never a frontier to build from — self-tested with an invalid binder yielding `halt` set and an empty `frontier`, and the self-test's [PASS] lines name that case with the fragment 'invalid-binder' and the forged-done provenance cases with 'forged-done'), `slug`, `default_branch` (detected the way Phase 1 already detects it), `integration_branch` {name, exists, tip}, `refs` (every refs/karta/<slug>/item-*/{built,failed,done,accepted,evidence} that exists, with its target), `wave_tags` (every karta/<slug>/wave-* tag), `done_provenance` (for EVERY item carrying a done ref: the result of `check_item_provenance.py --check-accepted --slug <slug> --item <id> --range <done>^1..<done>` (the merge commit plus its merged side — NOT `<base>..<done>`, which for any item merged after a wave-mate contains the wave-mate's commits and fails the checker's every-commit-carries-this-marker rule; reproduced during review with two parallel item branches) — the check Step 1 already requires before trusting a done item on resume; PLUS, for every done ref whether clean or accepted, a first-parent reachability check: the done target must appear in `git rev-list --first-parent karta/<slug>/integration` (measured today: the checker alone returns OK for a clean done ref pointing at an item commit never merged into integration, so this reachability rule is what catches a forged clean done) — any failure of either check is reported per item and sets the packet's `halt` field, and the deliver doctrine treats a packet with `halt` set as a stop, never as a frontier to build from (the deliver SKILL carries the literal fragment 'never as a frontier' beside that rule, and the oracle greps it) — the packet cannot make a forged `accepted`/`done` pair disappear behind a clean-looking frontier), `frontier` (the ready items — those not done whose dependencies all carry a done ref that passed done_provenance), `parallelism` {parallel: [ids], serialize: [ids], reasons: {id: [gate names]}} — a PARTITION of the frontier computed from the four deterministic gates in skills/_shared/parallelism-gates.md that a script can decide (a dependency edge, an explicit `serialize`, overlapping `touches`, a co-declared `shared_resources`); it never infers a gate from prose, and it says which gate put an item in `serialize`. The two gates a script cannot decide are handled CONSERVATIVELY, never dropped: when the binder's `env_contract.supports_isolation` is false, every frontier item whose oracle needs the environment (oracle `type` integration, e2e or visual) goes to `serialize` with reason `undecidable:stateful-env`; an item with no `touches` goes to `serialize` with reason `undecidable:missing-touches`. The packet lists these under `parallelism.unresolved` as well — a LIST of item ids, with the reasons staying in `parallelism.reasons`, and the deliver doctrine says the orchestrator may move such an item back to `parallel` only after reading the item plans the way Step 2 already requires — the packet never silently widens what runs together. Both cases are self-tested with a negative control (isolation true → parallel; touches present → parallel), as is resume provenance: a synthetic repo whose `done` ref points at a commit outside the integration branch's first-parent history — one case with an `accepted` ref alongside, one case as a plain clean done — each yields `halt` set, and a valid second done merge that follows another item's merge passes and that item absent from the frontier, while a genuine done merge passes. And `tools`: the ABSOLUTE resolved paths of run_oracle.py, scan_secrets.py, check_item_provenance.py and item_context.py, all resolved from this script's own location so a worktree, a plugin install and a repo checkout all work. The docstring carries the canonical namespace string 'refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/evidence' verbatim (shared term). work_items.title: The merge queue becomes one command per item
work_items.summary: A new script performs the pre-merge checks, the merge, the re-validation and the record for one item in a single call, closes a wave with explicit checks, and writes the wave tag only when the orchestrator says the wave is truly over.
work_items.contract: A NEW pure-stdlib script skills/karta-deliver/scripts/merge_item.py on the house pattern (argparse, `--self-test` with [PASS]/[FAIL] lines and an N/N summary, exit 0/1, `python3 <path>`), with three subcommands (`merge`, `close-wave`, `tag-wave`), plus the doctrine that invokes it. It depends on the preflight item because both edit skills/karta-deliver/SKILL.md. (1) `merge --repo <integration worktree> --binder PATH --slug S --item ID [--allow-drift]` performs today's Step 3 mechanically, STOPS AT THE FIRST FAILURE, and ALWAYS prints one fixed-shape JSON object on stdout: {item, skipped_done, provenance, drift, merge_commit, revalidation, done_ref, halted_at} — the same keys on every path, with `halted_at` naming the step that stopped it or null. In order: (a) DONE-REF IDEMPOTENCY, VERIFIED — if refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/done exists, it is trusted only after the same two checks preflight applies: `check_item_provenance.py --check-accepted` over `<done>^1..<done>` (the merge commit and its merged side; a wider range would contain wave-mates' commits and fail spuriously) and first-parent reachability of the done target from karta/<slug>/integration; both pass → skipped_done true, exit 0; either fails → `halted_at: \"done-provenance\"`, exit 1, nothing written — a worker sharing the ref namespace can write a done ref after preflight ran, and a skip must never take its word; this is resume-idempotency, not a race fix, since the queue is serial. (a2) PRECONDITIONS, checked before anything is touched — the integration worktree is CLEAN (`git status --porcelain` empty) and HEAD is `karta/<slug>/integration`; refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/built EXISTS and equals the item-branch tip, and no refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/failed ref is present. Any of these failing halts with `halted_at` naming it, exit 1, nothing written: a branch the gate halted (failed present, built absent or stale) reaches the tip only through a human accept at the Phase-4 halt, which this script never performs. The pre-merge tip is recorded now. (b) PROVENANCE — run check_item_provenance.py (path resolved from this script's location) WITHOUT --check-accepted over <integration-tip>..<item-tip>; a nonzero result halts before any merge. The accepted-state form belongs to resume and to the moment just after an accepted ref is written, and is not this subcommand's business. (c) DRIFT CHECK — read refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/evidence with `git cat-file` and compare the record's `command_sha256` with the sha256 of the binder oracle's current command — hashed over the exact command string bytes as stored in the binder JSON, UTF-8 encoded, no trimming or normalization, the same form run_oracle.py records (`_sha256_hex(command.encode("utf-8"))`), so the two sides can never disagree on canonicalization. A mismatch is reported as `drift: true` and HALTS unless --allow-drift is passed, because the binder's command changed since the item built and that is a human's call. A missing or unreadable ref is NOTED in the result and is never fatal — a read failure must not block a merge. The exact string 'refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/evidence' (shared term) and the exact string 'command_sha256' appear in the file. (d) MERGE — `git merge --no-ff` with the message `Merge item <id> into integration [karta:item-<id>]`, so the marker grammar the provenance checker already knows survives. A CONFLICT is a halt: `git merge --abort`, verify the tree is clean and HEAD is back at the recorded pre-merge tip, report `halted_at: "merge"` with the conflicting paths, exit 1 — a conflicted MERGE_HEAD must never be left for the next item to trip over. (e) RE-VALIDATION ALWAYS RE-EXECUTES — the exact lowercase fragment 'always re-executes' appears in the script and stays in the SKILL. Run run_oracle.py against the MERGED tip with the oracle's resolved cwd and expect, and put its capped record in `revalidation`. There is no skip-on-match: a matching command hash says nothing about the composed tree, which is what merge-time re-validation exists to test. On failure, first verify HEAD is still the just-made merge commit on `karta/<slug>/integration` (the only state a reset may destroy), then `git reset --hard` back to the recorded pre-merge tip, write NO done ref, and exit 1. (e2) CLEAN AND UNMOVED AFTER THE ORACLE — after re-validation, `git status --porcelain` must be empty again AND `git rev-parse HEAD` must still be the just-made merge commit with `karta/<slug>/integration` checked out (an oracle that runs `git reset`, `git checkout`, an empty commit or a ref update has moved the tip: `halted_at: \"tip-moved\"`, restore the recorded PRE-MERGE tip — a full unwind, so a resumed run re-merges from a known state instead of finding the item half-landed — exit 1, no done); close-wave verifies the branch and tip it started on are unchanged after every check, and tag-wave tags the explicitly resolved `refs/heads/karta/<slug>/integration` tip it read at entry; an oracle that left tracked modifications or new untracked files validated a tree that is not the merge commit, so this halts exactly like a failed oracle (`halted_at: \"dirty-after-oracle\"`), and the same rule applies to every `close-wave` check: close-wave requires a clean tree on entry, and on `dirty-after-check` it restores index and tracked tree with `git reset --hard HEAD` — which moves no ref, and unlike `git checkout -- .` also clears a STAGED mutation (a check that ran `git add` would otherwise leave the index dirty; reproduced during review) — then runs `git clean -fd`, so a mutating check never strands the worktree for the next merge — self-tested with a mutating check on both the passing and the failing path, including one that stages its modification. And close-wave's tip promise is enforced, not merely checked: it records the branch and tip at entry, and a check that MOVED them — a commit, a reset, a ref update or deletion, a detached HEAD — routes through the SAME shared five-step unwind back to the recorded entry tip and exits nonzero (`halted_at: "tip-moved"`), self-tested with one check that commits and one that deletes the integration ref, each restored on both the exit-0-then-rejected and the exit-nonzero path. ROLLBACK REMOVES WHAT IT CREATED: because (a2) proved the tree clean before anything ran, any untracked file present at rollback was created by the merge or the oracle — so a halt after the merge started does `git reset --hard <pre-merge tip>` AND `git clean -fd` (never -x: ignored files such as caches predate the run and are not the script's to delete — the literal `-fdx` never appears in the script, and the oracle greps for its absence), then verifies porcelain is empty. (f) On success `git update-ref refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/done <merge commit>` and record it. (2) `close-wave --repo … --binder … --slug S --check CMD [--check CMD …]` runs the post-wave check on the new tip — the project's build/type-check the orchestrator already resolved, passed explicitly with `--check` (required, repeatable; `env_contract.command` is the command that STARTS the environment and is never used here), each run through run_oracle.py with its capped record in the result — then skills/karta-plan/scripts/check_shared_terms.py (path resolved from this script's own location), whose result appears in the printed JSON under a `shared_terms` key — self-tested: a close-wave run's output carries the key. It writes NO tag and does NOT revert: reverting a wave rewinds refs and restores failed markers and stays a doctrine decision made with the human. It prints the result and exits nonzero on any failure. (2b) `tag-wave --repo … --slug S --wave N` writes karta/<slug>/wave-<N> at the current integration tip and nothing else; the doctrine invokes it ONLY after the wave's Phase-4 accept/defer decisions have resolved and a final close-wave has passed on the resulting tip — the success tag must point at the true wave tip, accepts included, exactly as Step 4 already says. (3) DELIVER DOCTRINE. skills/karta-deliver/SKILL.md Step 3 and Step 4 — and the two EXISTING `--check-accepted` invocations the file already carries (the resume check in Step 1 and the post-accept check in the Phase-4 accept flow), whose range is corrected from `<base>..<done>` to `<done>^1..<done>` for the same reason (reproduced during review: the wide range rejects a valid accepted item merged after a wave-mate because it sees the wave-mate's commits; and the accept merge MUST carry the item marker for this to hold: reproduced during review — an accept merge whose subject lacks `[karta:item-<id>]` fails the narrow range with 'no marker', a marked one passes. So Phase 4 step 2 of the accept flow and the Accept section of skills/_shared/integration-branch.md now require the accept merge to be made with `--no-ff` — a fast-forward leaves no merge commit to carry the subject, and `<done>^1..<done>` is then meaningless; the literal `--no-ff` appears in both the Phase-4 accept flow and the Accept section, and the oracle asserts it there — with the subject `Accept item <id> into integration [karta:item-<id>]` and the two Karta-Accepted trailers below it — the same marker grammar as the queue merge. Migration, stated in the doctrine: an accept merge made before this rule is unmarked, so a resumed delivery that contains one halts at done-provenance naming that cause; the way forward is Clear (the binder is re-delivered) — there is no re-stamping of history) — invoke the script (`merge`, then `close-wave` with the resolved floor as `--check`) and read its result, and the wave tag is written with `tag-wave` only after Phase 4 resolves, KEEPING every fragment slice 1 requires in this file: 'run_oracle.py', 'check_item_provenance.py', 'command_sha256', 'always re-executes'. Step 3's barrier text says: dispatch the wave's builds in the background and WAIT FOR THE HOST'S COMPLETION NOTIFICATIONS — never sleep-poll, never loop on refs (the measured run spent 7 turns waiting, each re-reading a 55–60k-token context; the exact lowercase fragment 'never sleep-poll' appears in the file). (4) skills/_shared/integration-branch.md's 'Serial merge queue' section names merge_item.py as how the queue is executed, without changing what the queue does; every per-skill copy stays byte-equal (check_shared_copies.py must report in sync). (5) MEASURED TARGETS, stated and not asserted: orchestrator merge-queue turns per item 5 → 1; post-wave turns 7 → 3 or fewer; waiting turns 7 → 0. (6) SELF-TEST, hermetic, each case with its negative control: build a temp repo with an integration branch, an item branch, an evidence ref written by run_oracle.py --attach-ref, and a binder carrying an oracle command; then prove — a clean merge writes the done ref and leaves a merge commit carrying the [karta:item-<id>] marker; a missing built ref, a built ref not at the item tip, a present failed ref, a dirty integration worktree and a HEAD not on the integration branch each halt before any merge with nothing written; a conflicting item branch is aborted, leaving a clean tree at the pre-merge tip and no done ref; an oracle that exits 0 but creates an untracked file halts as dirty-after-oracle with the file removed and no done ref, and an oracle that fails after creating an untracked file leaves a clean tree at the pre-merge tip; an oracle that exits 0 after `git reset --hard HEAD^` halts as tip-moved with the pre-merge tip restored and no done ref; an oracle that exits 0 after detaching HEAD (`git checkout --detach`) or switching to another branch while `karta/<slug>/integration` still points at the merge commit halts as tip-moved with BOTH the integration ref and the checked-out HEAD back at the recorded pre-merge tip, a clean tree, and no done ref — ONE SHARED UNWIND ROUTINE serves every halt after the merge started — a failing oracle, dirty-after-oracle, tip-moved, a failed verification — there is no second, older reset path; the routine is a FIXED, FORCED sequence that works from any state the oracle can leave: (1) `git update-ref refs/heads/karta/<slug>/integration <pre-merge tip>` — recreates the branch if the oracle deleted it, and is the only ref a rollback ever writes; (2) `git checkout -f karta/<slug>/integration` — forced, so a tracked modification the oracle made while a divergent foreign branch was checked out cannot make the checkout refuse (the foreign branch's ref is never written, so it keeps its tip; the self-test asserts that sha unchanged); (3) `git reset --hard <pre-merge tip>`; (4) `git clean -fd`; (5) verify HEAD, the integration ref and an empty porcelain, and halt loudly if verification fails. Self-test cases, each run TWICE — once with an oracle that exits 0 (rejected afterwards) and once with an oracle that exits nonzero — asserting the integration ref and HEAD at the pre-merge tip, empty porcelain, the foreign ref unchanged and no done ref: switched to a divergent foreign branch AND a tracked path modified; the integration ref deleted by the oracle; a done ref pointing off-chain halts as done-provenance instead of being skipped, while a genuine done merge that follows another item's merge is skipped cleanly, and an ACCEPTED done — a no-ff merge with the doctrine's real accept subject (marker plus the Karta-Accepted and Karta-Accept-Reason trailers) merged after a wave-mate — is skipped cleanly while the same accept merge without the marker halts; an oracle that fails on the merged tip resets the branch to the recorded pre-merge tip and writes NO done ref and exits 1; a drifted command_sha256 halts without --allow-drift and proceeds with it; an existing done ref makes the merge a no-op with skipped_done true; close-wave exits 0 when every --check passes and nonzero when one fails, and writes no tag on either path; tag-wave writes karta/<slug>/wave-<N> at the tip. The self-test's [PASS] lines NAME their cases with the exact lowercase fragments 'tip-moved', 'dirty-after-oracle', 'dirty-after-check', 'done-provenance', 'drift', 'staged', 'foreign', so the oracle holds the destructive negative controls to their names in the output rather than trusting a bare exit 0. (7) MIRRORS. Run `python3 scripts/sync_codex_skills.py` as the last step after the final canonical edit.

work_items.title: Every gate reviewer is handed the evidence instead of re-deriving it
work_items.summary: Each gate dispatch brief now carries the oracle's evidence record, the work item itself and the changed-file list, and both reviewers are told to read them rather than reconstruct the same facts from the repository.
work_items.contract: The change the user asked for, and the one place in this binder where the gates themselves change. (1) THE BRIEF. skills/karta-verify/SKILL.md, section `verify:brief`: EVERY gate dispatch brief — first dispatch as well as kickback, either agent, either mode — carries, in this order AFTER the existing `Diff-size:` line: an `Evidence-record:` line followed by the run_oracle evidence record JSON read from refs/karta/<slug>/item-<id>/evidence with `git cat-file` (when the ref is absent, the literal `Evidence-record: none` plus one clause saying why — an absent record is stated, never omitted); a `Work-item:` block holding the item's JSON slice (id, title, contract, oracle, touches, shared_resources, surface); and a `Changed-files:` block holding `git diff --stat <range>` followed by `git diff --name-status <range>`. The kickback rule is unchanged: deterministic facts only, never the prior attempt's verdict prose. (2) IT MUST NOT TRIP THE GUARD. hooks/scripts/guard_gate_dispatch.py reads the brief text before either context spins up. Two constraints the new blocks must respect, and they are not obvious: the guard takes the FIRST `<rev>..<rev>` token in the brief as the diff range, so the range line stays ahead of the new blocks; and it resolves the word `worktree` to a path, so the worktree-path line and the range line come FIRST: the guard resolves the first `worktree` mention that names an existing path and stops there, which is what makes a contract or evidence record that later mentions a worktree harmless. The oracle proves it the hard way — it runs the guard's own `decide()` against briefs that embed every REAL work-item JSON of this binder (contracts included) and an evidence record whose command contains the word worktree and a `..` token, for both agent types — and one malformed brief, its `Range:` line deleted, is asserted REFUSED (nonzero decide code): the guard must reject as well as accept. (3) THE ACCEPTANCE REVIEWER. In agents/karta-acceptance-reviewer.md (and therefore in the regenerated .codex/agents/karta-acceptance-reviewer.toml and the bundled skills/karta-verify/references/karta-acceptance-reviewer.agent.md): the evidence record becomes a NAMED input. The record is CURRENT only when ALL of these hold: its `command_sha256` equals the sha256 of the oracle `command` carried in the Work-item block; its `cwd` equals the item's resolved oracle cwd (the oracle's own `cwd` joined to the worktree, else the worktree root); its `expect` equals the oracle's declared expectation — same mode and same pattern, or both absent — and, when present, matched (a record whose expectation differs from the current oracle's is stale even if it matched its own); and its `tree_sha` equals the tree of the reviewed range's tip (`git rev-parse <tip>^{tree}`). The third binds the record to the exact content under review — `head_sha` cannot, because karta-build attaches the record at the clean floor BEFORE it commits, so in the measured run every record's head_sha was the item tip's PARENT. The agent text lists these four tests verbatim with a one-line reason each — carrying the exact plain-text strings `git rev-parse <tip>^{tree}`, `head_sha cannot decide currentness`, and (for the test-suite boundary below) `a passing exit status does not show what the test exercised`, which the oracle greps so the comparisons themselves are pinned, never just the field names — so a reviewer cannot pass a record whose command moved to another directory or whose marker changed. A record missing `tree_sha` (written by a pre-2.33 runner) or failing any test is STALE and settles nothing — say so and disposition as today. (2b) THE RUNNER GAINS `tree_sha`. skills/karta-build/scripts/run_oracle.py records a twelfth key, `tree_sha`: the `git write-tree` of the resolved cwd's repository working tree, computed through a temporary index (GIT_INDEX_FILE) populated with `git add -A` semantics so untracked files count and the real index is never touched; null outside a repository. The docstring's key count, the key list, and the self-test's exact-key-set check (`record has exactly eleven keys`, lines ~126/297/303 today) are all updated to twelve; every existing key keeps its meaning. Self-test additions with a negative control: a record written on a working tree that is then committed unchanged has tree_sha equal to `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`; after one more edit and commit the two differ; and the self-test stages a real index entry first, captures `git ls-files --stage` before and after the record, and asserts them byte-identical — the temporary index never leaks into the real one. A 9-recheck floor re-run after a kickback re-attaches the record, so a corrected diff carries a fresh tree_sha. When a CURRENT record reports `success: true`, that is the SETTLED disposition for the narrow class of assertions the shell command's own exit status or expect marker directly establishes (the self-test exits 0; the named string is present in the named file because the command greps it) — disposition those `covered-by-command`, citing the record, and do not re-derive them from logs. An assertion that a TEST the command runs establishes stays `covered-by-test`: the reviewer still opens the test body, because a passing exit status does not show what the test exercised. This is a new disposition alongside `covered-by-test` and `declared-debt`, and it narrows nothing else: inspection assertions are still judged by reading the diff hunks, contract conformance still needs an external artifact, and a record reporting `success: false` or a missing record settles NOTHING — it falls back to today's rules. The `Work-item:` block must name the same item as the brief's `Item:` line — a mismatch is a doctored brief and the verdict is BLOCKED, never a review of whichever block arrived. The reviewer reads the binder on disk ONLY when the brief carries no `Work-item:` block, so a directly-dispatched gate still works. (4) THE SAFETY AUDITOR. In agents/karta-safety-auditor.md and its two projections: take the blast-radius signal (signal 5) from the `Changed-files:` block rather than recomputing the file list — confirming it against the file headers of the diff hunks it reads anyway; a path in the diff that the block omits is BLOCKED (a doctored brief), never silently trusted — and keep reading the diff hunks for the other six signals and for the stack-pack check. Its inputs list gains the two new blocks. (5) BOTH AGENTS STAY READ-ONLY. `tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash` is unchanged in both files, and neither agent ever runs the oracle command — they read a record of a run someone else performed. The oracle asserts the tools line verbatim. (6) NO SLEEP-POLLING. `verify:parallel` says the dispatcher waits for both gates' completion notifications rather than polling; the literal `completion notifications` appears in the file. (7) PROJECTIONS. Run `python3 scripts/sync_codex_agents.py` then `python3 scripts/sync_codex_skills.py` after the final canonical edit — the bundled .agent.md files live inside karta-verify, so the skills mirror changes too. (8) MEASURED TARGETS, stated and not asserted: gate messages per context 4–6 → 3 or fewer; gate tool calls per gate pair 13–14 → 6 or fewer; gate cost per run $0.31 → $0.20 or less. The gates are 6.5% of the bill, so this item is judged on being right, not on its share of the saving.

work_items.title: The measured cost of a delivery is written down where a reader will find it
work_items.summary: The parallelism-and-review guide gains a short section with the measured per-role cost of a delivery and what each new command replaces, and the fixture README records that the miner now reports context and cost per role.
work_items.contract: Two prose edits, written last so they describe what actually landed. (1) docs/how-to/parallelism-and-review.md gains a section headed exactly 'What a delivery costs and where the turns go', after the existing parallelism section. It carries the measured table from the 2.32.0 fixture-v1 run — orchestrator 44 messages and 57% of a $4.82 run, builders 66 messages and 36%, the acceptance reviewers 3.5%, the safety auditors 3% — says in one plain sentence that the bill is context multiplied by turns because cache reads are about 90% of the billed tokens and cache traffic nearly all of the dollars, and then says what each new command replaces: deliver_preflight.py replaces the orientation the orchestrator used to do by hand, item_context.py replaces the search a builder used to run before its first edit, and merge_item.py replaces the per-item merge sequence. Keep it plain: this file is read by people using karta, not by people building it, so name the commands but do not explain their JSON. Follow the repo's plain-language rules for user-facing prose, and use markdown tables with the minimum separator. (2) benchmarks/perf/fixture-v1/README.md, in its 'After the run' section, notes that benchmarks/perf/mine_fixture.py now also reports context tokens and cost per role, and that cost figures need the run's headless result file passed with --result. The literals 'context tokens' and 'cost per role' appear there. (3) This item states the binder's target where a reader meets it: at least 40% below the 2.32.0 baseline of $2.41 an item on fixture-v1, judged by the perf-fixture-cost-baseline card run after the next release under the same resolved model-ID set as the 2.32.0 baseline (the card's own comparison precondition; a different model set is inconclusive for the target, not a pass or a fail) — written as the target it is, never as a result already achieved. (4) It depends on all four earlier items because it describes them; nothing here is written from the plan, only from what landed. The section states, verbatim and greppable: the run cost ($4.82 for two items, $2.41 an item), the three shares (57% orchestrator, 36% builders, 6.5% gates), that cache read tokens are about 90% of the tokens billed — with cache traffic, reads plus creation, nearly all of the spend — and the written-down target (40% lower cost per item — the unrounded cost_usd_per_item at or below 0.60 × $2.41 = $1.446 — judged only against an unchanged model-ID set); a section missing any of these fails the oracle.
